$comment: S3178 / S4029: the source-controlled boundary between the two Wear artifacts.
The `standard` flavor is what Google Play distributes and is an ALLOWLIST: a capability is absent from it
unless it is named under `standardAllowlist`. `noLegal` is the sideload artifact and keeps everything.
Every noLegal-only category below names the permissions, components and routes that carry it, so returning
one capability to the store variant is a reviewable edit of this file rather than a silent manifest change.
Read by scripts/quality/assert-wear-store-boundary.ps1, which judges the two merged manifests against it.
Version 2 (S4029, owner ruling 2026-10-01): the store build offers every capability Play permits on a watch;
only health and body data, credential entry, the automatic listening start and the screen takeover programs
stay sideload-only. The classification behind each answer is

standardAllowlist.$comment: The whole surface the store build offers. Nothing outside this list may appear in the standard merged manifest. S3555: POST_NOTIFICATIONS carries the stopwatch's WO-V4 indicator. S4029: media, microphone, network, radios, foreground location, foreground services and every entry-point component returned from the noLegal-only categories; each is listed under the capability it serves. An entry point survives hiding its screen, so a withheld command is also refused where it arrives - WatchWearListenerService refuses the distress-signal start and ResolveWearLaunchAddressUseCase refuses a withheld destination.

libraryContributed.$comment: Declarations no source file in this module writes - they arrive from a dependency manifest or from the debug build type. They are allowlisted by name rather than by a wildcard, so a library that starts contributing something sensitive still surfaces as an unnamed declaration. S3362: androidx.core's DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION is named twice because it is built from the applicationId, so the debug merge carries the `.debug.` infix and the RELEASE merge does not - allowlisting only the debug spelling failed the gate against the artifact that actually ships.

noLegalOnly.$comment: S4029: the S2941 start that raises the listening window through a full-screen intent and confirms it without a tap. Play admits USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT for alarms and calls, and an unprompted microphone start is unexpected sensitive access; the store build keeps listening behind the notification tap and Allow.

S2486 / S4029: typing a username and password on the watch, which WO-P6 refuses. The routes stay registered in both editions and the screen refuses itself where the answer is false; sources provisioned from the phone stay reachable.

Heart rate, blood pressure and activity/motion readings, and the Tourist dashboard S3042 gated with them. Already confined by S2457, S2458 and S2995; the owner named blood pressure as the example of what stays sideload-only (S4029).

S3362: the water flashlight and the distress signal. Both consume every pointer event on the initial pass so a wet wrist cannot dismiss them, which is the gesture WO-V3 asks for on almost every screen and neither of the two exemptions it names. They also draw full-bleed white against WO-V13, and the signal raises the alarm stream to its maximum and strobes at about three flashes a second. No permission carries either one - the screens ARE the capability. S4029: the phone's distress-signal start is refused by the Data Layer listener as well, now that the store build declares it. The shade lock (locksSystemShade) belongs to the flashlight and stays sideload-only with it.
